method.scope: Saved TensorBoard scalars and native training JSONL, iterations1-25, before LEFT optimizer restore defect.
method.sample_alignment: Each update collects4096 transitions in both arms; compare at identical cumulative steps.
method.scalar_aggregation: RewardComponentsCallback logs each finite component from each sampled step with reduce=mean, window=100; RLlib merges runner metrics and TensorBoard records float32 scalars. These are smoothed runner aggregates, not exact means over4096 transitions.
method.clip_lift_identity: mean(base_clipped) - [0.2 mean(actual_score) +0.8 mean(served_score) -mean(base_penalty)]. Linear recombination preserves a shared averaging operator; it does NOT apply clip to the mean raw base.
method.interpretation: With nonnegative scores/penalties, blends summing to1 and clip bounds[0,1], upper clipping cannot activate. Positive clip lift measures weighted aggregate upward correction from negative raw bases. It does not reveal number, duration or locations of clipped steps.
method.cross_check: Mean reward equals mean base minus the sum of active post-clip terms within float32 precision. This supports aligned averaging of relevant component streams; raw early transition traces are unavailable.
method.window_summary: Five-iteration table entries are arithmetic means of the five logged smoothed values, not pooled step means or episode-return estimates.

left.limitation: Different target/normalization and visited states; score values across arms are not common physical quality metrics.

right.limitation: Different target/normalization and visited states; score values across arms are not common physical quality metrics.

conclusion: Early base clipping is real and materially changes aggregate scalar values in both arms. Mature-rollout clipping findings cannot be generalized to initial learning.
RIGHT has larger initial clip lift than LEFT yet subsequently better completion; current evidence does not identify clipping as a selective LEFT failure mechanism.
Initial command-rate cost is almost identical in both arms and dominates base penalty. Whether it blocks recovery corrections is not determined by these smoothed aggregates.
LEFT has better imitation-score aggregates while worse completion later; target-specific normalized scores do not rank cross-task physical robustness.
